title: Cohort resurrection scheduler with criterion-driven rollforward
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: recovery playbooks for quarantined cohorts have been manual and error-prone. This PR introduces a 'Cohort Resurrection Scheduler' that automates safe re-introduction (resurrection) of previously-quarantined cohorts and provides a criterion-driven rollforward path for cohorts that passed smoke and fidelity checks after quarantine. The goal is to reduce toil, shorten mean-time-to-recover healthy cohorts, and provide deterministic bisect-friendly replays for post-rollback promotion.

What this change does (single continuous description): Implements a scheduler and associated controller that can: 1) snapshot cohort state at quarantine time (traffic fraction, session anchors, telemetry anchors), 2) run deterministic replay dry-runs against a shadow lane to verify fixes, 3) run a tiered re-introduction (micro-bisect -> smoke -> progressive ramp) when safety criteria are met, 4) provide a rollforward decision engine that evaluates rolling windows of latency/error/fidelity metrics and promotes or re-quarantines cohorts automatically. Includes UX hooks for the Console, observability additions, and an ops playbook for manual override.

Key design notes: - Resurrection is opt-in per rollout via a new rollout.policy.resurrection stanza in the API; default is disabled to avoid accidental re-promotes. - The scheduler keeps immutable snapshots so resurrection can be replayed deterministically. - Criterion-driven rollforward uses configurable gates: latency P95, error rate, semantic-fidelity regression (delta vs baseline), and sample-level smoke tests. Each gate declares a threshold and an enforcement action (continue/promote/quarantine). - Integration points: Release Conductor (for orchestration), KV cache snapshot metadata, and telemetry service for near-real-time metrics. - Safety: All promotions apply a conservative backoff with exponential cooling and a maximum retry window. The system stores a resurrection ledger for audit and automatic revert.

Checklist: - [x] Controller + scheduler implementation (rollout/controller/resurrection_scheduler.go) - [x] API schema additions and validation (api/rollouts.proto) - [x] Deterministic replay harness + tests (tests/integration/resurrection_e2e_test.go) - [x] Console UI (console/pages/rollouts/resurrection-ui.tsx) - [x] Metrics & tracing (telemetry/metrics/rollout_metrics.md) - [x] Ops playbook (ops/playbooks/cohort-resurrection.md) - [x] Documentation (docs/rollouts/resurrection-scheduler.md)

Commits (high level): - feat(rescheduler): add resurrection scheduler and state snapshotting - feat(api): add resurrection policy proto and validation - feat(replay): deterministic replay harness and micro-bisect driver - feat(console): resurrection UI and manual override controls - test: e2e tests for smoke and progressive ramp - docs: ops playbook and rollout docs

Files changed (high level): - rollout/controller/resurrection_scheduler.go (core scheduler, snapshot and state machine) - api/rollouts.proto (resurrection policy, gating schema) - replay/driver/micro_bisect.go (deterministic bisect/replay logic) - telemetry/metrics/rollout_metrics.md (new metrics and dashboards) - console/pages/rollouts/resurrection-ui.tsx (UI and manual controls) - ops/playbooks/cohort-resurrection.md (runbook + rollback steps) - tests/integration/resurrection_e2e_test.go (integration scenarios) - docs/rollouts/resurrection-scheduler.md (design + config examples) - infra/helm/values-rollout.yaml (feature flag toggle and defaults)

Testing and CI: All unit tests and integration e2e passed in CI (see ci_checks). Local soak: staged on perf-canary with a small synthetic cohort; observed no regressions in tail latency and a ~1.7% reduction in manual operator time to recover cohorts during the week-long trial.

Rollout plan: feature gated in main via the infra/helm toggle. Initial deployment to Canary, then to Dedicated control-plane, and optionally enabled in Private via operator opt-in. Default policy is disabled; product teams opt in per rollout.

Operational notes & playbook summary: The ops playbook documents manual steps to abort resurrection, force-quarantine, or fast-forward a resurrection to a full promote if necessary. The resurrection ledger is queryable and recorded in audit logs for compliance.

Why unique / tradeoffs: This approach avoids blind automatic promotes by having a deterministic replay step and explicit gates. Tradeoffs include added complexity to the rollout controller and additional storage for snapshots, but the operational ROI is positive for customers with frequent transient regressions.

Related work: References ENG-3482 (resurrection strategy spike) and ENG-3640 (deterministic replay harness). Links to internal design doc: Linear ENG-3482 (attached).

release_notes: Adds an opt-in Cohort Resurrection Scheduler to safely reintroduce quarantined cohorts via deterministic replay and configurable gates. Feature is disabled by default and can be enabled per-rollout via api/rollouts.proto resurrection policy. Includes UI, telemetry, and ops playbook.
